key_insight: Target-aligned input reparameterization (TAIR) makes neural surrogates for real-fluid thermodynamics easier to learn by replacing raw enthalpy with thermodynamically matched ideal-gas estimates.
engineering_relevance: This can cut the cost of real-fluid property evaluation in supercritical combustion solvers while preserving accuracy for temperature, density, and compressibility closures.
method: Use a constant-cp ideal-gas enthalpy inversion to generate a target-aligned temperature input for the T network.
Use ideal-gas density estimates as inputs for the density and compressibility networks.
Train surrogates to learn real-fluid departures from ideal-gas baselines instead of reconstructing the full thermodynamic closure from raw (h,p,Y).
evidence_signal: Against raw-input and cross-reparameterization controls on supercritical methane-oxygen counterflow flame data, TAIR reduced held-out RMSE by about 1.5x for T, 2.0x for ρ, and 7.5x for ψ, with even larger gains on an unseen strain-rate flame.
watch_item: TAIR depends on the quality of the ideal-gas baseline and species constants, so mismatched thermodynamic assumptions or extrapolation beyond the augmented envelope may limit robustness.
paper_title: Thermodynamics-Informed Input Reparameterization for Neural Prediction of Real-Fluid Thermodynamic Properties in Supercritical Combustion
